cells.tense: Right now, with the pen in your hand
cells.verb: seeing what's actually there before you've decided what it means
cells.place: in the thing you're tending while it grows
cells.ask: let one clear noticing out loud, as a gift rather than a correction — and watch how the seeing holds its own light when it isn't trying to prove anything
cells.core:
You're looking at what's growing under your care and seeing it as it is, not as you planned it. That first clean look — before advice, before worry, before you know what it adds up to — is doing the real tending. The thing you're caring for gets to be met, not managed.

There's room here to go one step further: say one thing you see, plainly, to whoever or whatever is growing, and not to steer it. Just because you saw it. Clear seeing shared that way doesn't push; it lights the room, and the growing thing finds its own way by it.
cells.sheetLine: You see what's growing as it is, and that's the care.

cells.tense: You're bracing against a future you can't read yet
cells.verb: looking too hard for what the first shoots mean
cells.place: over the thing you're tending while it grows
cells.ask: come to it today as if you've never seen it before — carry only what it has actually become, not what you've forecast — and the seeing turns back into light instead of a search
cells.core:
You're bracing against a future you can't read yet. Every small change in what you're tending gets held up and read as a sign of where it's heading, and the reading is running ahead of the growing. Looking that hard, that early, cuts into things that weren't ready to be cut.

The way back isn't to look less. It's to arrive fresh: stand in front of what you're caring for and take in only what's there now, what it has actually become, with no story about tomorrow attached. Beginner's eyes. That kind of seeing is warm rather than sharp — you see because you're looking, not because you're trying to prove you saw it coming.
cells.sheetLine: You're reading the future into every new leaf.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that's already behind you
cells.verb: not really looking at what's growing anymore
cells.place: in the care you're still giving but no longer watching
cells.ask: pick one thing you've already chosen to do for what you're tending and carry it all the way to done; the looking comes back on the far side of the finishing, and so does the light that doesn't have to prove itself
cells.core:
You're still standing at a door that's already behind you. You're tending, but you're tending the version from before — the one you last really saw — and the fresh look hasn't been taken in a while. The care continues; the seeing has gone quiet.

Don't force yourself to look. That rarely works, and it isn't where the current is. Instead, take one thing you've decided to do for what's growing and finish it, start to end, chosen rather than dutiful. Completing something real pulls your attention back into the present, and the clear seeing returns on its own — the kind that shines because you're here, not because you had to prove you were paying attention.
cells.sheetLine: You're caring for what you last saw, not what's there.

cells.tense: You've put the pen down in a room you're already writing in
cells.place: in the way your care keeps adjusting to it
cells.ask: say one thing you've noticed about what you're tending, out loud, as something you saw — and let it be yours, plainly, with nothing to prove
cells.core:
You've put the pen down in a room you're already writing in. Your care keeps adjusting to what's growing — you notice when something shifts and you respond to it — but you'd call it the thing's own doing, or luck, or just how it went. The seeing is happening. The credit isn't landing on the one who sees.

The move is small and earlier than it sounds: say what you noticed. Not what to do about it, not why it matters. Just the noticing, named as yours. Clear seeing owned that simply doesn't swell into pride; it's light because you're looking, and the thing you're tending grows better in a room where someone admits they can see it.
cells.sheetLine: You already see it. You keep saying the thing just happened.
